item.title: “Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both,…
item.description:
“Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both, and experiences mental suffering and mental distress. When craving is abandoned, one does not plan for one’s own harm, nor for others’ harm, nor for the harm of both, and does not experience mental suffering or mental distress. Thus, brahmin, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.53

item.title: “Monk, cultivate seclusion, Do not be heedless, Do not let your mind whirl in sensual pleasures. If you are heedless, you will swallow a hot…
item.description:
“Monk, cultivate seclusion,
Do not be heedless,
Do not let your mind whirl in sensual pleasures.
If you are heedless, you will swallow a hot iron ball,
And when burned, do not cry out in pain!”

“Without wisdom, there is no jhāna;
Without jhāna, there is no wisdom.
One who has both jhāna and wisdom
Is indeed close to Nibbāna.”

“Entering an empty house,
A monk with a peaceful mind
Experiences a superhuman delight
In the clear vision of the Dhamma.”

“When he clearly comprehends
The arising and passing away of the aggregates,
He gains joy and rapture —
That is the deathless for those who know.”

From: Dhammapada 360-382

item.title: “Rāhula, when you wish to perform a bodily action, you should reflect upon that same bodily action: ‘Would this bodily action that I wish to…
item.description:
“Rāhula, when you wish to perform a bodily action, you should reflect upon that same bodily action: ‘Would this bodily action that I wish to do lead to my own harm, to the harm of others, or to the harm of both? Then this bodily action is unwholesome, leading to suffering, resulting in suffering.’ If, on reflection, you know: ‘This bodily action that I wish to do would lead to my own harm, to the harm of others, or to the harm of both; it is unwholesome, leading to suffering, resulting in suffering’—then such a bodily action you should certainly not do. If, on reflection, you know: ‘This bodily action that I wish to do does not lead to my own harm, nor to the harm of others, nor to the harm of both; it is wholesome, leading to ease, resulting in ease’—then such a bodily action you should do.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 61 – Ambalaṭṭhikārāhulovādasutta

item.title: “Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With…
item.description:
“Monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties, virtue is destroyed. With no virtue, with deficiency in virtue, right concentration is destroyed. With no right concentration, with deficiency in right concentration, true knowledge and vision are destroyed. With no true knowledge and vision, with deficiency in true knowledge and vision, disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed. With no disenchantment and dispassion, with deficiency in disenchantment and dispassion, the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed. Just as, monks, a tree with deficient branches and foliage — its shoots do not reach perfection, its bark does not reach perfection, its sapwood does not reach perfection, its heartwood does not reach perfection. So too, monks, with unguarded faculties, with deficiency in guarding the faculties … the knowledge and vision of liberation are destroyed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.50

item.title: - “Wonderful, Venerable Kaccāna! Marvelous, Venerable Kaccāna! The way Venerable Kaccāna has defined non-guarding of the sense faculties is excellent. Venerable Kaccāna has spoken of…
item.description:
- “Wonderful, Venerable Kaccāna! Marvelous, Venerable Kaccāna! The way Venerable Kaccāna has defined non-guarding of the sense faculties is excellent. Venerable Kaccāna has spoken of ‘guarding of the sense faculties, guarding of the sense faculties.’ To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the sense faculties?” - “Here, brahmin, a monk, when seeing a form with the eye, his mind does not incline toward agreeable forms nor recoil from disagreeable forms. He dwells with mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. When he hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … feels a touch … cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, his mind does not incline toward agreeable phenomena nor recoil from disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. Thus, brahmin, is the guarding of the sense faculties.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.132
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, whatever is greed — that is unwholesome. Whatever a person does bodily, verbally, or mentally with greed — that is unwholesome. When a person…
item.description:
“Monks, whatever is greed — that is unwholesome. Whatever a person does bodily, verbally, or mentally with greed — that is unwholesome. When a person with greed, overcome by greed, with mind uncontrolled, makes another suffer — by killing, binding, confiscation, abuse, or expulsion — thinking ‘I am strong, I have power’ — that is unwholesome. Thus, many evil, unwholesome states arise in him born of greed, originating from greed, produced by greed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.69

item.title: “Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with…
item.description:
“Monks, form is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … disenchanted with feeling … disenchanted with perception … disenchanted with formations … disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, there is knowledge: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.15

item.title: - “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.…
item.description:
- “Wonderful, Venerable Bharadvāja! Marvelous, Venerable Bharadvāja! This is well spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. This very cause, this very reason, Venerable Bharadvāja, is why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, do not indulge in sensual pleasures and live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully. I too, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body unguarded, speech unguarded, mind unguarded, mindfulness unestablished, sense faculties unrestrained — then lust overcomes me. But, Venerable Bharadvāja, when I enter the inner apartments with body guarded, speech guarded, mind guarded, mindfulness established, sense faculties restrained — then lust does not overcome me.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.127
